question: What is the primary benefit of early antenatal booking in Nigerian midwifery practice?

options.A: Eliminates the need for any laboratory tests later
options.B: Establishing a health baseline and catching risks early
options.C: Guarantees a completely complication-free delivery
options.D: Permits immediate transfer of care to a tertiary hospital

explanation: Early booking gives the midwife a clear picture of the mother's health status, allowing for timely prevention and management of potential complications. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why does managing low-risk pregnancies at primary healthcare centers matter for the health system?

options.A: It stops pregnant women from traveling to rural areas
options.B: It ensures that doctors perform all routine check-ups
options.C: It completely removes the cost of childbirth for families
options.D: It prevents tertiary facilities from becoming overcrowded

explanation: Filtering low-risk clients to primary centers keeps referral hospitals free to handle severe, complex emergencies that truly require specialist care. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which measurement on a first-trimester ultrasound gives the most accurate estimate of gestational age?

options.A: Abdominal circumference
options.B: Femur length measurement
options.C: Crown-rump length
options.D: Biparietal diameter

explanation: Crown-rump length measured during the first trimester has the smallest margin of error for dating a pregnancy accurately. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h2)

question: A woman states her last menstrual period began on September 10th of last year. Using Naegele's rule, what is her expected date of delivery?

options.A: July 17th
options.B: June 3rd
options.C: June 17th
options.D: May 17th

explanation: Adding seven days to September 10th gives September 17th, adding a year gives September 17th of next year, and subtracting three months brings you to June 17th. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which past surgical procedure carries the highest direct risk of uterine rupture in a future labor?

options.A: Uncomplicated open cholecystectomy
options.B: Previous classical caesarean section
options.C: Excision of an external skin cyst
options.D: Appendectomy performed in childhood

explanation: A classical vertical uterine scar has a significantly higher risk of rupturing during labor compared to a lower transverse scar. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why must a midwife carefully review a client's past obstetric history during the first booking visit?

options.A: It determines the biological sex of the unborn baby
options.B: Past complications like hemorrhage often repeat in future pregnancies
options.C: It proves whether the mother attended antenatal care previously
options.D: It is required to calculate the exact crown-rump length

explanation: Obstetric complications such as severe bleeding or recurrent miscarriages provide vital clues about risks in the current pregnancy. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically evaluated as part of a socio-economic and environmental antenatal screening?

options.A: Presence of domestic stress or partner support
options.B: Distance and transport to the health facility
options.C: Fetal chromosomal anomaly markers
options.D: Stability of housing and daily nutrition

explanation: Chromosomal markers are biological and genetic indicators assessed via ultrasound or blood tests, not socio-economic or environmental factors. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do long distances to healthcare facilities directly affect rural pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: They prevent the midwife from performing accurate urine dipstick tests
options.B: They guarantee that the baby will be born with a low birth weight
options.C: They automatically increase the biological risk of gestational diabetes
options.D: They delay timely access to emergency care during sudden complications

explanation: Long travel distances combined with poor transport options can turn manageable emergencies into fatal delays when labor complications strike. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which finding during an early booking visit requires immediate referral to a specialist obstetrician?

options.A: History of three consecutive spontaneous miscarriages
options.B: Mild morning sickness settling with simple diet changes
options.C: A mild history of seasonal allergic rhinitis
options.D: A normal body mass index recorded at booking

explanation: Recurrent miscarriages indicate an underlying medical or anatomical issue that requires specialist investigation and management. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h5)

question: A woman booking at eight weeks shows signs of severe lower abdominal pain and spotting, with no intrauterine gestational sac seen on ultrasound. What is the most appropriate midwifery action?

options.A: Advise her to increase her heavy physical labor to clear the pelvis
options.B: Refer her urgently for suspected ectopic pregnancy evaluation
options.C: Reassure her that spotting is completely normal and send her home
options.D: Book her for a routine return visit in four weeks' time

explanation: Severe pain, spotting, and an empty uterus on ultrasound are classic warning signs of an ectopic pregnancy, which is a surgical emergency. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is risk stratification considered a continuous, ongoing process throughout pregnancy rather than a one-time event?

options.A: Ministry of health guidelines require paperwork to be updated weekly
options.B: New complications can develop at any stage after the initial booking
options.C: Mothers often change their place of residence mid-pregnancy
options.D: The gestational age changes every week, invalidating the first scan

explanation: A pregnancy that starts out entirely normal can develop conditions like pre-eclampsia or fetal growth restriction later on, requiring reclassification. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of antenatal care visits for a family stratified into low-risk community care?

options.A: Frequent surgical interventions and continuous intravenous therapy
options.B: Restriction from all physical activity and household chores
options.C: Daily specialist blood pressure monitoring in a tertiary ward
options.D: Wellness promotion, routine monitoring, and birth preparation

explanation: Low-risk care centers on supporting normal physiological processes, educating the family, and preparing for a safe delivery. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What best describes true informed consent in midwifery practice?

options.A: A legal document signed quickly by the husband without discussion
options.B: The absolute refusal of any medical advice by the family
options.C: A collaborative dialogue where the client understands options and risks
options.D: An oral agreement made only when a complication becomes severe

explanation: Informed consent is built on open communication, ensuring the mother fully comprehends her care plan before agreeing to it. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h7)

question: How does a strong therapeutic alliance directly improve pregnancy outcomes?

options.A: It completely prevents the occurrence of genetic fetal abnormalities
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory investigations or scans
options.C: It ensures the baby is delivered exactly on the estimated due date
options.D: It encourages the mother to share concerns and return for scheduled visits

explanation: When a pregnant woman trusts her midwife, she is more open about symptoms and more likely to maintain consistent antenatal attendance. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T1#BMP321_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a primary advantage of conducting home visits during pregnancy?

options.A: It reduces the overall cost of hospital equipment.
options.B: It reveals actual living conditions and daily realities.
options.C: It guarantees a completely complication-free delivery.
options.D: It replaces the need for standard laboratory tests.

explanation: Home visits allow midwives to see environmental and social factors firsthand that clinics cannot show. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h1)

question: How does visiting a pregnant woman at home change the professional relationship?

options.A: It removes the need for professional boundaries.
options.B: It establishes the midwife as a strict legal authority.
options.C: It makes the client responsible for clinical diagnoses.
options.D: It positions the midwife as an accessible health partner.

explanation: Entering the home shifts the dynamic away from an intimidating clinic setting toward a collaborative partnership. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h1)

question: Who should a midwife always contact first when entering an unfamiliar community?

options.A: International aid workers
options.B: Local community leaders and elders
options.C: The closest private pharmacy owner
options.D: National security officials

explanation: Respecting local leadership structures ensures community acceptance and protects the safety of the midwife. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife arrives in a village for home visits and immediately starts walking door-to-door without notifying anyone. What is the main risk of this approach?

options.A: It can cause suspicion and resistance from residents.
options.B: It prevents the midwife from writing clinical notes.
options.C: It breaks strict international midwifery laws.
options.D: It will automatically invalidate any collected data.

explanation: Failing to notify local authorities or community leaders often leads to distrust and uncooperative residents. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h2)

question: How should a midwife respond when a client mentions a traditional belief that contradicts medical advice?

options.A: Listen actively and gently negotiate safe practices.
options.B: Scold the client for following unscientific ideas.
options.C: Threaten to withhold all future medical care.
options.D: Ignore the comment and change the subject immediately.

explanation: Respectful dialogue and gentle education build trust far better than harsh criticism or immediate dismissal. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following actions best demonstrates cultural sensitivity during a home visit?

options.A: Insisting that only English is spoken inside the house
options.B: Rushing through the conversation to save clinical time
options.C: Observing local customs like removing shoes at the door
options.D: Refusing to sit on traditional furniture offered by the family

explanation: Small acts of respect, such as following household etiquette, show cultural humility and foster strong rapport. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a major health hazard associated with indoor cooking using unvented firewood?

options.A: Complete depletion of body iron stores
options.B: Respiratory distress and smoke inhalation
options.C: Rapid onset gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Sudden adult hearing loss in pregnant women

explanation: Heavy smoke from biomass fuels irritates the respiratory tract and poses significant risks to both mother and baby. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h4)

question: During a home visit, a midwife notices that the family drinks untreated water from a nearby stream. What is the most appropriate initial recommendation?

options.A: Provide them with expensive bottled water for the rest of the pregnancy.
options.B: Advise the family on safe water boiling or treatment methods.
options.C: Tell them to immediately move to a different neighborhood.
options.D: Report the entire family to the local environmental sanitation board.

explanation: Practical, low-cost interventions like boiling water are realistic solutions that families can readily adopt. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to include key family decision-makers in birth preparedness discussions?

options.A: They are legally required to sign all midwifery case notes.
options.B: They often control access to funds and emergency transport.
options.C: They pay the midwife's salary directly after delivery.
options.D: They perform the physical clinical examinations at home.

explanation: Because family members frequently hold financial and logistical power, their buy-in is essential for emergency planning. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical focus when assessing family support structures?

options.A: Measuring the exact square footage of the family land
options.B: Determining who makes financial decisions for medical care
options.C: Identifying who will help with household chores after birth
options.D: Recognizing key relatives involved in maternal care

explanation: Social support assessment focuses on people, relationships, and decision-making dynamics rather than land measurements. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h5)

question: A midwife arrives for a scheduled home visit and senses that the immediate neighborhood has become dangerously tense and volatile. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Ignore the tension and proceed with a loud megaphone.
options.B: Withdraw from the area immediately and reschedule later.
options.C: Argue with local youths to assert professional authority.
options.D: Enter the house quickly and lock all the doors from inside.

explanation: Personal safety always comes first; a midwife should never compromise physical safety to complete a routine visit. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which action violates professional ethics during a community home assessment?

options.A: Partnering with a local community health worker for introductions
options.B: Writing down environmental observations in the official case record
options.C: Wearing an official identification badge while walking through the village
options.D: Discussing a client's private financial struggles with clinic staff for gossip

explanation: Sharing private family details outside of direct clinical necessity breaches patient confidentiality and professional trust. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h6)

question: When should a midwife document the findings from a community home visit?

options.A: Only if the client develops a severe complication
options.B: When the woman eventually arrives for her postpartum check
options.C: Immediately after leaving the home environment
options.D: At the end of the calendar month during audit

explanation: Prompt documentation prevents memory lapse and ensures accurate records are available for future clinic visits. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h7)

question: How do home visit records improve longitudinal care in the antenatal clinic?

options.A: They prove that the midwife completed community work quotas.
options.B: They exempt the client from paying any standard hospital fees.
options.C: They link home realities directly to ongoing clinic consultations.
options.D: They replace all physical examinations performed by the doctor.

explanation: Recording environmental and social findings allows the clinical team to provide context-aware care throughout pregnancy. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T2#BMP321_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the booking visit in antenatal care?

options.A: To deliver the baby immediately if complications arise
options.B: To discharge the mother from routine hospital follow-up
options.C: To schedule the exact date and time of spontaneous labor
options.D: To establish a comprehensive health profile and identify risks

explanation: The booking visit gathers baseline health data so midwives can spot potential complications early and plan safe care. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must midwives adjust their approach when a pregnant woman books very late in her pregnancy?

options.A: By focusing immediately on critical health investigations and risk screening
options.B: By skipping physical examinations and relying entirely on her age
options.C: By refusing care until she brings a letter from her community leader
options.D: By referring her straight to a tertiary teaching hospital without assessment

explanation: Late presentation means less time for routine spacing, so urgent baseline checks take priority to protect mother and baby. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which action best helps build trust during the first antenatal consultation?

options.A: Sitting at eye level and using respectful, culturally sensitive language
options.B: Standing over the desk to maintain professional clinical authority
options.C: Interrupting frequently to speed up the documentation process
options.D: Keeping the examination door wide open for easy staff passage

explanation: Equal eye contact and culturally appropriate respect put the mother at ease, encouraging honest sharing of health details. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h2)

question: A newly booked teenager appears silent and avoids eye contact when asked about her pregnancy. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Scold her for wasting valuable time during a busy clinic day
options.B: Reassure her of confidentiality and use a gentle, welcoming tone
options.C: Call security to ensure she answers all clinical questions truthfully
options.D: Write down that she is non-compliant without asking further questions

explanation: Fear and shame are common in young mothers; reassuring them of privacy helps lower their anxiety. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h2)

question: What does 'parity' refer to when taking an obstetric history?

options.A: The number of deliveries past 28 weeks of gestation
options.B: The total number of living children in the household
options.C: The total number of times a woman has ever conceived
options.D: The exact age of the mother at her first delivery

explanation: Parity specifically counts viable births or deliveries reaching the age of viability, distinct from total pregnancies. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is a past history of uterine surgery important to note during booking?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born prematurely
options.B: It automatically prevents the mother from experiencing morning sickness
options.C: It increases the risk of uterine rupture in subsequent labors
options.D: It eliminates the need for routine blood pressure checks

explanation: Scars on the uterus from prior surgeries like myomectomy or cesarean sections can weaken the muscular wall under labor stress. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which physical finding is a major risk factor for cephalopelvic disproportion during booking?

options.A: Mild swelling of the fingers in hot weather
options.B: Short maternal stature below 150 cm
options.C: Healed abdominal scars from childhood surgery
options.D: A slight increase in baseline pulse rate

explanation: Height under 150 cm often correlates with a small pelvis, raising the risk of obstructed labor. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is checking the conjunctiva for pallor an essential part of the baseline physical exam?

options.A: To screen for maternal anaemia, which is highly prevalent
options.B: To diagnose gestational diabetes mellitus accurately
options.C: To determine the exact fetal heart rate pattern
options.D: To test the visual acuity of the pregnant woman

explanation: Conjunctival pallor is a quick clinical sign that suggests low hemoglobin levels requiring prompt investigation. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary reason midwives screen for domestic challenges during antenatal care?

options.A: It helps doctors decide which patients receive free medications
options.B: Hospital management requires complete financial audits of every family
options.C: Social factors strongly influence maternal and fetal health outcomes
options.D: Midwives are legally mandated to report all marital disagreements

explanation: Stress, abuse, and poverty directly affect a pregnant woman's health and ability to carry a pregnancy safely. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h5)

question: How should a midwife approach screening for domestic violence?

options.A: By asking direct, confidential, and non-judgmental questions
options.B: By assuming educated women never experience domestic issues
options.C: By asking the husband to confirm if his wife is being abused
options.D: By waiting until visible bruises appear during labor

explanation: Private and gentle questioning is necessary because victims rarely volunteer information about abuse spontaneously. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which symptom is a key indicator of potential antenatal depression?

options.A: Persistent sadness and feelings of hopelessness
options.B: Increased frequency of daytime urination
options.C: Mild fatigue during the first trimester
options.D: Occasional cravings for unusual local foods

explanation: Depression goes beyond normal pregnancy tiredness, marked by ongoing low mood, despair, and loss of interest in daily life. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to actively screen for mental health issues during antenatal visits?

options.A: Mental health screening replaces the need for blood pressure checks
options.B: Hormones guarantee that every pregnant woman develops clinical psychosis
options.C: It is only done to fulfill administrative paperwork requirements
options.D: Emotional distress can negatively affect birth outcomes and self-care

explanation: Untreated depression or anxiety can lead to poor nutrition, missed appointments, and increased risks for low birth weight. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which laboratory test is routinely performed at booking to check for infection risks like syphilis and HIV?

options.A: Liver function test
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Serology screening
options.D: Sputum microscopy

explanation: Serology tests screen for blood-borne and sexually transmitted infections that can harm the developing fetus if left untreated. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is determining the Rhesus factor at the first antenatal visit vital?

options.A: To prevent complications related to Rhesus blood group incompatibility
options.B: To calculate the exact date of spontaneous rupture of membranes
options.C: To determine whether the mother will need a cesarean section
options.D: To check if the mother has an active urinary tract infection

explanation: Knowing Rhesus status allows midwives to provide anti-D immunoglobulin to Rhesus-negative mothers, preventing hemolytic disease in newborns. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary output of synthesizing all baseline assessment findings?

options.A: An individualized care plan tailored to the mother's specific needs
options.B: A standard discharge paper releasing her from further clinics
options.C: An immediate order for hospital admission until delivery
options.D: A permanent diagnosis that cannot be changed later

explanation: Bringing all findings together allows the midwife to design a safe, personalized schedule of care and interventions. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h8)

question: A woman is booked at 20 weeks with severe anaemia and a history of two previous stillbirths. What should her care plan prioritize?

options.A: Frequent specialist reviews, iron therapy, and high-risk monitoring
options.B: No intervention until she goes into spontaneous active labor
options.C: Routine discharge to a primary health post with annual visits
options.D: Advice to stay at home and avoid visiting any health facility

explanation: Her history of stillbirths and severe anaemia classifies her pregnancy as high risk, requiring close clinical oversight. [learn more](BMP321_U1_T3#BMP321_U1_T3_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of booking a pregnant woman for antenatal care as early as possible?

options.A: To establish a baseline of her health and plan her care
options.B: To register her for hospital security protocols
options.C: To determine the exact sex of the baby early
options.D: To force her to buy antenatal drugs immediately

explanation: Early booking allows midwives to record baseline vital signs, lab results, and health history so they can spot any changes later in the pregnancy. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h1)

question: A woman comes for her first booking visit at 28 weeks. Why is checking her Packed Cell Volume (PCV) immediately so important?

options.A: To measure the amount of amniotic fluid around the fetus
options.B: To calculate her exact expected date of delivery
options.C: To detect and treat baseline anemia before labor approaches
options.D: To check if she has eaten enough food before coming

explanation: Anemia is common and dangerous during childbirth, so knowing her PCV early gives the midwife time to correct it before delivery. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h1)

question: What measurement is used during a first-trimester ultrasound to give the most accurate gestational age?

options.A: Biparietal Diameter
options.B: Femur length size
options.C: Abdominal circumference
options.D: Crown-Rump Length

explanation: Measuring the embryo from the top of its head to its buttocks in the first trimester gives the most precise dating. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why might relying solely on Naegele's Rule sometimes give an inaccurate due date in clinical practice?

options.A: Hormonal changes in the third trimester alter the calculation
options.B: Babies always arrive exactly on the calculated day without fail
options.C: The rule only works if the mother is under twenty years old
options.D: Many women cannot accurately remember their last menstrual period

explanation: Naegele's rule depends entirely on an accurate recall of the last menstrual period, which many patients forget or confuse with implantation bleeding. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which specific instrument is traditionally used by midwives to listen to the fetal heart beat during routine visits?

options.A: Standard adult stethoscope
options.B: Pinard stethoscope
options.C: Electronic sphygmomanometer
options.D: Neonatal pulse oximeter

explanation: The Pinard stethoscope is a classic, reliable acoustic horn designed specifically to listen to the fetal heart through the maternal abdomen. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h3)

question: During a routine visit at 34 weeks, a midwife performs abdominal palpation. What is the primary purpose of using Leopold's maneuvers at this stage?

options.A: To stimulate the uterus and check if labor is about to start
options.B: To push a breech baby into a head-down position immediately
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the baby down to the gram
options.D: To determine the position, presentation, and lie of the fetus

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers use systematic hand placements on the mother's abdomen to feel how the baby is lying inside the uterus. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h3)

question: At what gestational age does the symphysio-fundal height in centimeters generally equal the gestational age in weeks?

options.A: 40 weeks
options.B: 12 weeks
options.C: 24 weeks
options.D: 16 weeks

explanation: From 24 weeks onwards, the fundal height in centimeters matches the weeks of pregnancy quite closely during normal fetal growth. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h4)

question: What should a midwife suspect first if a woman at 32 weeks has a symphysio-fundal height measuring only 27 centimeters?

options.A: The baby is definitely going to be born overdue
options.B: Possible fetal growth restriction or incorrect dating
options.C: Normal twin pregnancy with extra fluid accumulation
options.D: The mother has been eating too much carbohydrate

explanation: A measurement significantly lagging behind the expected weeks often points to growth restriction, low amniotic fluid, or a miscalculated due date. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why does a pregnant woman experience a natural drop in her hemoglobin concentration during the second trimester?

options.A: Kidneys excrete protein and red blood cells into the urine
options.B: Bone marrow temporarily stops producing new cells during gestation
options.C: The growing fetus consumes all the iron stores in the liver
options.D: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell count

explanation: The fluid portion of blood expands significantly during pregnancy to support the placenta, diluting the concentration of red blood cells. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following clinical findings in a pregnant client is considered PATHOLOGICAL rather than a normal adaptation?

options.A: Slight shortness of breath when walking up a flight of hospital stairs
options.B: Frequent urination during the first and third trimesters of pregnancy
options.C: Mild swelling in the ankles and feet after standing for a long time
options.D: Swelling that spreads to the face and hands accompanied by high blood pressure

explanation: Facial swelling and high blood pressure are classic warning signs of pre-eclampsia, unlike simple dependent ankle swelling. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h5)

question: What condition should a midwife suspect if a pregnant client complains of severe frontal headaches and blurred vision in her third trimester?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Normal migraine
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Pre-eclampsia

explanation: Persistent headaches and visual changes are neurological symptoms caused by severe hypertension and reduced blood flow to the brain in pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard warning sign that a pregnant woman should report immediately to the clinic?

options.A: Sudden swelling of the face and hands overnight
options.B: Mild morning nausea during the first trimester weeks
options.C: Any amount of bright red bleeding from the vagina
options.D: Complete absence of fetal movement for several hours

explanation: Morning sickness is a very common and usually benign symptom of early pregnancy, whereas bleeding, swelling, and reduced fetal movement are dangerous red flags. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of the mother-held antenatal card used in Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: It ensures the pregnant woman carries her medical history with her wherever she goes
options.B: It allows the government to track the exact population growth rate
options.C: It serves as a receipt for all payments made at the hospital pharmacy
options.D: It acts as an official birth certificate for the baby before delivery

explanation: Carrying her own records allows any healthcare provider at any facility to instantly see her booking data, blood group, and past complications. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h7)

question: A woman is referred from a primary health clinic to a teaching hospital because of severe pre-eclampsia. Why is clear documentation on her card critical at this moment?

options.A: It replaces the need for the new doctors to ask her any questions
options.B: It gives the ambulance driver directions on the fastest route to take
options.C: It proves to the tertiary hospital accountants that she paid her bills
options.D: It enables the receiving doctors to understand immediate treatments already given and act fast

explanation: Clear notes on blood pressure readings and drugs administered prevent delayed or duplicated treatment in an emergency referral. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T1#BMP321_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness in midwifery?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine antenatal blood investigations
options.B: To guarantee a completely pain-free delivery at home
options.C: To reduce delays in seeking and receiving emergency obstetric care
options.D: To transfer all financial burdens entirely to local government councils

explanation: BPCR specifically targets the well-documented delays that prevent women from accessing timely life-saving interventions during childbirth. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h1)

question: When should a midwife ideally begin discussing birth preparedness with a pregnant woman?

options.A: During the immediate third-stage delivery phase
options.B: At the first postnatal clinic appointment
options.C: During early antenatal booking visits
options.D: Only when true labor contractions start

explanation: Starting discussions early ensures there is ample time for the family to plan, save money, and address potential logistical hurdles long before term. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component typically found in an individualized birth plan?

options.A: A detailed schedule for the child's future secondary school enrollment
options.B: Arrangements for emergency transportation and fuel money
options.C: The name of a pre-identified compatible blood donor
options.D: The name and location of the chosen health facility for delivery

explanation: Birth plans focus exclusively on immediate pregnancy, labor, and postnatal logistics and safety, not long-term upbringing plans. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h2)

question: A primigravida at 28 weeks gestation asks why her birth plan needs to include a pre-identified blood donor. What is your best response as her midwife?

options.A: Severe bleeding can happen unexpectedly, and having a ready donor saves precious time.
options.B: The hospital blood bank requires a family member to replace every routine IV fluid bag.
options.C: Blood donation is used to boost the mother's immune system during the final trimester.
options.D: It is a legal requirement enforced by the government to register the baby's birth.

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is unpredictable and rapid; pre-arranging a blood donor prevents fatal delays in blood transfusion access. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which symptom in a pregnant woman strongly suggests impending eclampsia and requires immediate facility attendance?

options.A: Mild, intermittent lower back pain
options.B: Severe frontal headache and blurred vision
options.C: Increased appetite and mild weight gain
options.D: Frequent urination during the first trimester

explanation: Severe headaches and visual changes are classic warning signs of severe pre-eclampsia that can quickly progress to convulsions. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is teaching a pregnant woman to monitor fetal movements an essential part of complication readiness?

options.A: It helps detect potential fetal distress or intrauterine compromise early.
options.B: It guarantees that the baby will be born on the exact estimated due date.
options.C: It prevents the mother from experiencing gestational diabetes mellitus.
options.D: It replaces the need for standard electronic fetal heart rate auscultation.

explanation: A sudden reduction in fetal activity is often a sensitive, early warning sign that the fetus is experiencing distress in utero. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why should emergency funds for childbirth be kept entirely separate from daily household money?

options.A: To prevent the traditional birth attendant from seizing the family's savings
options.B: To prevent the emergency cash from being accidentally spent on routine daily needs
options.C: To satisfy strict banking regulations required for issuing birth certificates
options.D: To ensure the money earns higher interest rates in a commercial bank account

explanation: Separating emergency funds ensures that transport or drug fees remain immediately accessible when an unexpected crisis arises. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h4)

question: A pregnant woman living in a remote rural community expresses worry about reaching the clinic at night. What practical resource mobilization step should her midwife recommend?

options.A: Rely entirely on luck that an ambulance will pass by her house during the night
options.B: Advise her to stay inside her home and deliver unassisted if labor starts after dark
options.C: Instruct her to wait until morning light before seeking any form of medical attention
options.D: Pre-arrange an agreement with a trusted local vehicle driver and keep emergency fuel ready

explanation: Securing a reliable nighttime transport option beforehand eliminates critical delays in reaching a skilled facility during nocturnal labor. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h4)

question: Who is classified as a skilled birth attendant during childbirth?

options.A: A village spiritual leader who offers prayers for safe delivery
options.B: A traditional birth attendant who uses herbal mixtures and massage
options.C: Any elderly female relative with extensive experience delivering grandchildren
options.D: An accredited professional such as a midwife, nurse, or doctor with midwifery skills

explanation: Skilled birth attendants have formal medical training and the certified competencies required to manage normal deliveries and handle obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important for a woman with a known high-risk pregnancy to plan delivery at a tertiary or secondary facility?

options.A: Tertiary hospitals are always located closer to rural villages than local health posts.
options.B: Routine home deliveries are legally banned for all women residing in urban areas.
options.C: Secondary facilities charge no money for any drugs or medical consumables used.
options.D: Higher-level facilities have blood banks and surgical theaters ready for emergencies.

explanation: High-risk pregnancies require immediate access to advanced medical interventions like blood transfusions and surgery that primary or home settings lack. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it beneficial to include family elders or partners in birth planning discussions?

options.A: It forces the woman to abandon all her personal cultural preferences completely.
options.B: It builds a supportive network that facilitates quicker decision-making during emergencies.
options.C: It ensures that hospital staff do not need to communicate directly with the mother.
options.D: It legally transfers all medical liability for the pregnancy to the extended family.

explanation: Involving key family decision-makers early prevents hesitation and conflict when urgent medical approvals or funds are needed during a crisis. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h6)

question: A husband insists that his wife should deliver at home with a traditional herbalist, contrary to her high-risk birth plan. As her midwife, what is your best initial approach?

options.A: Engage both of them in a respectful counseling session to discuss the specific risks and explore his concerns.
options.B: Threaten to report the husband immediately to local law enforcement authorities for child endangerment.
options.C: Ignore the husband's opinion completely because only the pregnant woman's consent matters legally.
options.D: Dismiss the couple from the clinic and refuse to provide any further antenatal care services.

explanation: Respectful engagement and patient education help address underlying fears and foster collaborative family support for safe facility delivery. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical tool used by midwives to monitor the active progress of labor and detect deviations early?

options.A: The household budget sheet
options.B: The postnatal ledger
options.C: The partograph
options.D: The immunization card

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress, maternal condition, and fetal well-being, helping identify abnormal deviations promptly. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h7)

question: What action should a midwife take immediately when intrapartum monitoring reveals severe fetal distress?

options.A: Instruct the birth companion to collect more funds from home before offering care
options.B: Execute the emergency birth plan protocol, provide stabilization, and arrange prompt referral
options.C: Wait until the shift changes before informing the attending physician about the finding
options.D: Advise the mother to walk briskly around the hospital compound to ease the stress

explanation: Prompt action and adherence to the emergency protocol are vital to prevent severe neonatal asphyxia or intrapartum stillbirth. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary complication that makes the fourth stage of labor particularly hazardous for the mother?

options.A: Delayed breastmilk production
options.B: Chronic postnatal hypertension
options.C: Primary postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: The immediate postpartum period carries a high risk of excessive uterine bleeding due to uterine atony or retained placental tissue. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is postpartum emergency readiness emphasized even after a normal, uncomplicated delivery?

options.A: Life-threatening complications like postpartum hemorrhage can still occur suddenly after birth.
options.B: Neonates frequently develop severe infections within the first ten minutes of life.
options.C: Midwives need extra time to complete administrative paperwork and tally fees.
options.D: Mothers are legally required to remain admitted in the hospital ward for exactly two weeks.

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage and other emergencies can strike unexpectedly during the fourth stage, requiring constant monitoring regardless of how normal labor was. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T2#BMP321_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the main reason a midwife prepares a warm, draft-free delivery room before the birth?

options.A: To prevent the newborn from developing hypothermia
options.B: To help the placenta separate faster in the third stage
options.C: To keep the sterile instruments from rusting too quickly
options.D: To make the mother sweat less during active pushing

explanation: Newborn babies lose heat very quickly in cold environments, so keeping the delivery room warm protects them from dangerous drops in body temperature. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these items is typically found inside a standard sterile delivery pack?

options.A: Neonatal stethoscope
options.B: Intravenous cannula
options.C: Episiotomy scissors
options.D: Blood pressure cuff

explanation: A standard sterile delivery pack specifically holds surgical instruments required for the birth itself, such as clamps, cord scissors, and episiotomy scissors. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h1)

question: What information does abdominal palpation primarily give the midwife during admission?

options.A: Exact cervical dilation in centimetres
options.B: Foetal lie, presentation, and position
options.C: Exact time the true labour pains started
options.D: Mother's current blood sugar level

explanation: Abdominal palpation lets the midwife feel how the baby is lying inside the uterus before doing an internal exam. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why does a midwife review the woman's antenatal card immediately upon admission?

options.A: To identify baseline health values and risk factors early
options.B: To check if she paid her health insurance fees in full
options.C: To calculate the total hospital bills for the delivery
options.D: To find out if she attended all her scheduled clinic dates

explanation: The antenatal card contains vital past history like blood group and lab results that help the midwife anticipate potential complications. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h2)

question: How often should the foetal heart rate be checked during the active phase of normal labour?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Only when pushing starts
options.C: Every thirty minutes
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Checking the baby's heart rate every half hour helps catch signs of distress quickly during active labour. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h3)

question: What does crossing the alert line on a partograph generally tell the midwife to do?

options.A: Perform an immediate caesarean section without checking anything else
options.B: Stop all monitoring procedures and let labour proceed naturally
options.C: Transfer the woman to a facility with a doctor for closer supervision
options.D: Discharge the woman home because labour is moving too slowly

explanation: The alert line warns that labour is slower than normal, signaling the need for evaluation or referral before the action line is reached. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h3)

question: How does severe fear and anxiety directly affect a woman's physical progress in labour?

options.A: It immediately lowers the mother's blood glucose level
options.B: It releases stress hormones that can slow down contractions
options.C: It forces the cervix to dilate too fast within minutes
options.D: It causes the baby to turn into a breech presentation

explanation: High anxiety triggers catecholamine release, which can uncoordinate uterine activity and prolong the first stage of labour. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered a non-pharmacological pain relief method?

options.A: Oral tablets of strong opioids
options.B: Intravenous injection of pethidine
options.C: Epidural anaesthesia in the spine
options.D: Sacral counter-pressure and back rubs

explanation: Non-pharmacological techniques rely on physical touch, movement, and breathing rather than drugs to ease discomfort. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h4)

question: What clinical event marks the official start of the second stage of labour?

options.A: Start of regular painful contractions
options.B: Appearance of the bloody show
options.C: Rupture of the amniotic sac
options.D: Full dilation of the cervix

explanation: The second stage spans from the moment the cervix is fully dilated at 10 centimetres until the baby is completely born. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why does a midwife sometimes ask a pushing mother to pant when the baby's head is crowning?

options.A: To slow down the birth and prevent severe perineal tearing
options.B: To push the placenta out before the baby's shoulders emerge
options.C: To give the mother a chance to drink some oral rehydration fluids
options.D: To help the baby take its very first breath of air early

explanation: Panting stops forceful pushing for a moment, allowing the tissues to stretch gently and avoiding sudden tears. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the very first action a midwife performs on the baby right after birth?

options.A: Drying the baby thoroughly with a warm towel
options.B: Weighing the infant on a digital maternity scale
options.C: Giving an intramuscular injection of vitamin K
options.D: Giving the first dose of oral polio vaccine

explanation: Thorough drying removes wet amniotic fluid, prevents rapid heat loss, and stimulates the baby to start breathing well. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why does the midwife check around the baby's neck immediately after the head is born?

options.A: To see if there is any birthmark on the skin folds
options.B: To measure the exact length of the infant's neck
options.C: To check if the umbilical cord is wrapped around it
options.D: To check if the collarbone was broken during delivery

explanation: A nuchal cord occurs when the umbilical cord loops around the baby's neck, which the midwife must check and manage safely. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of performing AMTSL after delivery?

options.A: To help the baby pass the first stool
options.B: To speed up the healing of episiotomy
options.C: To make the mother produce milk faster
options.D: To prevent heavy bleeding after birth

explanation: AMTSL is a key intervention designed specifically to lower the risk of postpartum haemorrhage. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which uterotonic drug is standard for AMTSL given within one minute of delivery?

options.A: Magnesium sulphate
options.B: Hydralazine
options.C: Metoclopramide
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin 10 international units is the drug of choice for AMTSL because it works quickly with minimal side effects. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must a midwife carefully inspect the maternal surface of a delivered placenta?

options.A: To measure the total volume of blood lost during labour
options.B: To calculate the exact gestational age of the baby born
options.C: To check if the baby had a twin sibling in the uterus
options.D: To ensure no cotyledons or pieces of tissue are left inside

explanation: Missing pieces on the maternal side indicate retained placental tissue, which can cause severe bleeding and infection. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h8)

question: What part of the placenta shows if any fetal blood vessels tore off abnormally?

options.A: Umbilical root
options.B: Maternal side
options.C: Decidual plate
options.D: Fetal surface

explanation: The fetal surface displays the chorionic plate and branching blood vessels, where the cord inserts and membrane edges are checked. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h8)

question: How often should vital signs and uterine tone be checked in the first hour after delivery?

options.A: Every fifteen minutes
options.B: Every hour on the hour
options.C: Every four hours
options.D: Once before the shift ends

explanation: Checking every 15 minutes during the first hour allows midwives to detect early signs of postpartum bleeding or shock. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h9)

question: What benefit does immediate skin-to-skin contact provide to a newborn baby?

options.A: Prevents the baby from crying during the night hours
options.B: Makes the baby grow taller than normal during infancy
options.C: Helps regulate body temperature and stabilizes breathing
options.D: Ensures the baby will never catch childhood infections

explanation: Mother's body heat warms the baby naturally and helps keep vital physiological signs stable. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T3#BMP321_U2_T3_h9)

question: How long does the formal postnatal period typically last after childbirth?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Six months

explanation: The puerperium runs from the delivery of the placenta until six weeks postpartum. This is the timeframe needed for most maternal organs to return to their non-pregnant state. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is postnatal care scheduled as several visits rather than just a single check?

options.A: Government policy requires patients to visit the clinic daily.
options.B: Midwives have too many patients to see in one day.
options.C: Babies take a long time to learn how to feed properly.
options.D: Complications can develop gradually over weeks after birth.

explanation: Conditions like postpartum hemorrhage, infection, and mood changes can appear at different times, making multiple scheduled check-ins necessary. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main reason for checking the uterus frequently during the first two hours after birth?

options.A: To determine when the mother can walk home
options.B: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the baby
options.D: To check if the mother is hungry

explanation: A firm, contracted uterus compresses the open blood vessels at the placental site, which stops bleeding and prevents hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h2)

question: A new mother has a full bladder, and her uterus feels soft and pushed to the right. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the operating theater for an emergency surgery
options.B: Administer an intravenous infusion of oxytocin
options.C: Apply a tight abdominal binder immediately
options.D: Assist her to pass urine to empty her bladder

explanation: A full bladder prevents the uterus from contracting properly. Emptying the bladder usually resolves this uterine atony. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h2)

question: At which specific postnatal milestone is the comprehensive final routine check typically scheduled?

options.A: Day seven
options.B: Week six
options.C: Month three
options.D: Day three

explanation: The six-week visit is the standard final milestone where overall recovery, family planning, and baby growth are thoroughly evaluated. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a major clinical focus during the early postnatal visit around Day 3?

options.A: Checking the baby for adult tooth eruption
options.B: Fitting the mother for a permanent contraceptive coil
options.C: Assessing breastfeeding attachment and infant feeding
options.D: Performing a routine cervical smear test

explanation: The third day coincides with milk coming in, making it a critical time to correct latch issues before sore nipples or poor feeding develop. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the medical term for the normal vaginal discharge that occurs after childbirth?

options.A: Leukorrhea
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Lochia
options.D: Smegma

explanation: Lochia is the shedding of the uterine lining after delivery. It normally progresses from red to pink and finally to whitish-yellow. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h4)

question: By what postpartum timeframe should the uterus normally shrink back into the pelvis and no longer be felt on the abdomen?

options.A: Three days
options.B: Twenty-four hours
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: Six weeks

explanation: Involution proceeds rapidly so that by around the tenth to fourteenth day, the fundus sinks below the pelvic brim and is no longer felt on the abdomen. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following clinical signs is most indicative of a postpartum uterine infection?

options.A: Pain-free white vaginal discharge
options.B: Fever and foul-smelling lochia
options.C: Soft and painless calf muscles
options.D: High blood pressure and blurred vision

explanation: Infection inside the uterus causes a systemic fever and produces offensive, foul-smelling lochial discharge. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What condition should you suspect if a postnatal mother complains of sudden calf swelling and tenderness in one leg?

options.A: Normal postpartum fluid retention
options.B: Uterine subinvolution
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Postpartum depression

explanation: Unilateral leg pain, swelling, and redness are classic warning signs of a blood clot in the deep veins of the lower extremity. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the expected maximum weight loss percentage for a healthy newborn in the first week of life?

options.A: Zero percent
options.B: Twenty-five percent
options.C: Ten percent
options.D: Fifty percent

explanation: Initial weight loss up to 10% is normal due to loss of excess fluid and passing meconium, after which weight should steadily increase. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is exclusive breastfeeding recommended for the first six months of an infant's life?

options.A: Babies cannot digest any solid food until they reach one year of age.
options.B: Water given to babies always causes severe dental cavities.
options.C: Formula milk is completely unavailable in local markets.
options.D: Breast milk provides complete nutrition and immune protection without needing other fluids.

explanation: Breast milk contains all necessary nutrients, antibodies, and water required for the infant's growth and defense against infections during the early months. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of the mild condition known as 'baby blues'?

options.A: Spontaneous resolution within two weeks
options.B: Severe permanent delusions and hallucinations
options.C: Feeling anxious during the first few days
options.D: Mild tearfulness and emotional mood swings

explanation: Hallucinations and delusions do not occur in baby blues. Their presence indicates a severe condition like postpartum psychosis. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h7)

question: How can you best help a mother who shows signs of postpartum depression?

options.A: Prescribe sleeping tablets without consulting a doctor
options.B: Tell her to stop worrying because every new mother feels tired
options.C: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately to restore her hormones
options.D: Provide empathetic listening, involve family support, and refer her for professional care

explanation: Postpartum depression is a medical condition requiring validation, family support, and formal psychological or psychiatric intervention. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which vaccines are routinely administered to a newborn baby immediately at birth?

options.A: BCG and Oral Polio Vaccine
options.B: Measles and Yellow Fever
options.C: Diphtheria and Pertussis booster
options.D: Tetanus toxoid and Malaria vaccine

explanation: Newborns routinely receive the BCG vaccine for tuberculosis protection and the first dose of oral polio vaccine right after birth. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why is family planning counselling necessary during the early postnatal period?

options.A: Breastfeeding mothers cannot get pregnant under any circumstances.
options.B: Women are legally required to use contraception for two years.
options.C: Ovulation can occur and result in pregnancy before menstrual periods return.
options.D: Hospitals need to control population growth statistics.

explanation: A woman can release an egg and become pregnant before she sees her first postpartum menstrual period, making early advice essential. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of documenting clinical findings in the mother's and baby's health records?

options.A: To ensure continuity of care across different healthcare providers
options.B: To fulfill a decorative requirement for office shelves
options.C: To calculate the annual budget for the health facility
options.D: To provide reading material for incoming hospital visitors

explanation: Accurate records allow any midwife or doctor attending the mother or baby later to see past problems, treatments, and ongoing needs. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h9)

question: You assess a postnatal mother and find signs of severe postpartum hemorrhage that cannot be managed locally. What action should you take first?

options.A: Wait until the routine six-week checkup to report the finding
options.B: Stabilize the mother and activate the emergency referral pathway
options.C: Discard the patient records and close the clinic early
options.D: Advise the family to buy traditional herbs from the local market

explanation: Life-threatening complications require immediate stabilization and urgent transfer to a higher-level facility following established referral protocols. [learn more](BMP321_U2_T4#BMP321_U2_T4_h9)

question: What is the main reason student midwives keep an expectant family logbook?

options.A: Replacing hospital registers with student-generated records
options.B: Fulfilling a purely administrative duty without clinical value
options.C: Connecting classroom theory with practical clinical encounters
options.D: Testing the student's ability to perform major surgeries alone

explanation: The logbook acts as a bridge, helping student midwives apply lecture notes to real patients in the ward. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why does the logbook ask you to follow a mother and baby through the whole reproductive cycle?

options.A: To guarantee the birth happens without any complications
options.B: To simplify the hospital's official filing system
options.C: To prove the student worked night shifts in the ward
options.D: To demonstrate understanding of continuity of care

explanation: Following a family through antenatal, labor, and postnatal care shows that you can provide complete, unbroken care. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h1)

question: How do you keep patient details private when writing in your student logbook?

options.A: Replacing real names and hospital numbers with initials or serial numbers
options.B: Asking the village head to verify the patient's identity in writing
options.C: Storing the original hospital case files inside the student's personal locker
options.D: Sharing full patient details on social media groups for peer review

explanation: Using initials instead of real names protects patient privacy and ensures details cannot be traced back to an individual. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What does informed consent mean when an expectant mother takes part in your case report?

options.A: She agrees willingly after understanding the process and knows she can withdraw anytime
options.B: She must sign the form because the doctor ordered her to do so
options.C: She signs a legal contract binding her to the hospital for five years
options.D: She is paid a financial allowance for allowing the student to document her

explanation: Informed consent means the mother understands what is involved, agrees freely, and can stop participating at any time. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which tool is essential for recording the active phase of labor in your records?

options.A: The immunization card
options.B: The partograph
options.C: The surgical safety checklist
options.D: The daily dietary timetable

explanation: The partograph is the standard chart midwives use to monitor labor progress and maternal and fetal well-being. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must logbook entries follow a strict order from booking to postnatal care?

options.A: To ensure the book has an equal number of pages for every single section
options.B: To make it easier for the printer to bind the final hardcover document
options.C: To match the exact filing order used by the hospital's pharmacy department
options.D: To clearly show the natural progression and continuity of maternal health

explanation: Arranging records chronologically mirrors the real journey of pregnancy, making it easy to follow the clinical story. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h3)

question: How should a student choose the right patient for a case report?

options.A: Pick an anonymous patient from a textbook rather than a real clinical encounter
options.B: Select the patient with the longest hospital stay regardless of whether anything interesting happened
options.C: Pick a case that offers clear educational value, such as a distinct complication or well-managed delivery
options.D: Choose a pediatric surgical patient to show versatility outside of maternity care

explanation: A good case report highlights clinical problem-solving and practical midwifery skills in action. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h4)

question: What should you avoid doing when writing the case presentation section of your report?

options.A: Copying long paragraphs of general disease definitions straight from a textbook
options.B: Detailing the specific emergency interventions performed by the ward team
options.C: Listing the laboratory test results obtained during admission
options.D: Describing the patient's actual presenting complaints and vital signs

explanation: Case reports should focus on the actual patient's unique experience rather than filling space with generic textbook definitions. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the very first step in the midwifery care plan framework?

options.A: Implementation
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Assessment is where you start by gathering all necessary information and vital signs from the mother. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h5)

question: A student sets a goal for a new mother to breastfeed without pain within 48 hours. Which care plan phase is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Implementation
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Setting goals and deciding what outcomes to work toward happens during the planning phase. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is personal reflection an important part of a midwifery case report?

options.A: It provides legal protection against malpractice claims in the hospital
options.B: It proves the student spent more time writing than actually working in the clinic
options.C: It replaces the need for clinical supervisors to grade the student's practical skills
options.D: It encourages critical thinking and helps the student identify areas for professional growth

explanation: Reflecting on your practice helps you evaluate your performance and learn from clinical experiences to improve future care. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h6)

question: What type of information do you look at when analyzing newborn outcomes in your logbook?

options.A: The educational background of the newborn's father
options.B: The distance from the patient's house to the primary health center
options.C: Apgar scores, birth weight, and general newborn adaptation
options.D: The total cost of antenatal drugs bought at the pharmacy

explanation: Neonatal outcomes focus directly on the baby's health status right after birth and during the early newborn period. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is using correction fluid (tipp-ex) discouraged in clinical and student records?

options.A: It violates international rules regarding stationery color choices
options.B: It takes too long to dry before the next shift takes over
options.C: It raises suspicion of data tampering and makes the original entry unreadable
options.D: It smells too strongly for pregnant women in the antenatal ward

explanation: Official records must be clear and transparent. Errors should be crossed out with a single line so the original writing remains visible. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the main danger of writing up your clinical notes long after the event has passed?

options.A: Running out of blue ink in the student's ballpoint pen
options.B: Causing the patient's medical insurance policy to expire
options.C: Forgetting critical clinical details and recording incorrect event timelines
options.D: Making the handwriting too neat for the examiner to read

explanation: Waiting too long to document care relies on memory, which can lead to missed details and wrong timestamps. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h7)

question: What must be included in your logbook before you present it to external examiners?

options.A: Signatures from clinical preceptors and academic supervisors
options.B: A receipt showing purchase of the student's uniform
options.C: A passport photograph of the newborn's grandmother
options.D: The personal phone number of the hospital director

explanation: Supervisors must sign your records to verify that you actually performed the clinical duties under proper guidance. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why do training schools have strict formatting and binding rules for project logbooks?

options.A: To increase the financial profit of the campus photocopy shop
options.B: To test whether students know how to operate a commercial sewing machine
options.C: To make the books heavy enough to stay open on a desk without a paperweight
options.D: To maintain professional presentation standards and ensure durability during grading

explanation: Neat binding shows professionalism and keeps pages from falling out while multiple examiners review your work. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T1#BMP321_U3_T1_h8)

question: What does 'family dynamics' mainly describe in healthcare?

options.A: The physical size of a family home
options.B: The genetic history of inherited diseases
options.C: The pattern of interactions and power relationships within a household
options.D: The total monthly income earned by family members

explanation: Family dynamics focus on how people within a home relate to each other, communicate, and share responsibilities, which affects health choices. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why should a midwife consider a pregnant woman's household, not just the woman alone?

options.A: Midwives are legally required to document financial status
options.B: Domestic relationships and living situations heavily influence her health choices and outcomes
options.C: Hospital management mandates a complete family tree
options.D: Extended family members pay all hospital bills

explanation: A pregnant woman's decisions and access to care are shaped by the people she lives with, making the wider family vital to her well-being. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of these describes a common household structure in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Strictly nuclear units where grandparents never reside
options.B: Extended family networks and polygamous compounds
options.C: Isolated single-room urban apartments with no relatives
options.D: Communal village dormitories managed by the government

explanation: Many Nigerian homes involve extended family systems and polygamous setups where multiple generations live and interact closely. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h2)

question: How can household decision-making patterns affect a woman's access to maternity care?

options.A: Traditional rulers must personally escort every expectant mother
options.B: Financial control and permission to seek care often rest with senior family members
options.C: Government policy requires the oldest child to approve appointments
options.D: Midwives are legally barred from speaking to anyone except the husband

explanation: Because power often lies with household heads or elders, a woman may need their approval and funds before she can visit a clinic. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a health benefit of a supportive family during pregnancy?

options.A: Higher rates of untreated postpartum eclampsia
options.B: Improved emotional well-being for the expectant mother
options.C: Better compliance with scheduled antenatal visits
options.D: Lower levels of maternal stress and anxiety

explanation: A supportive environment helps prevent poor outcomes rather than causing severe medical conditions like untreated eclampsia. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant woman arrives with severe bleeding, and her mother-in-law insists she drink an herbal remedy first. What does this show?

options.A: How household hierarchies can cause dangerous delays in emergency care
options.B: An ideal protocol for managing bleeding in rural health posts
options.C: The successful integration of herbal medicine into standard hospital care
options.D: A minor domestic disagreement with no clinical safety impact

explanation: Relying on traditional remedies first due to family pressure creates critical delays in receiving professional medical treatment for emergencies. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is a primary financial barrier for disadvantaged households regarding maternity care?

options.A: An excess of free ambulances in rural areas
options.B: Mandatory government health insurance for all citizens
options.C: Too many health facilities operating in every village
options.D: Lack of money for transport and clinic fees

explanation: Financial constraints and the cost of transportation are major hurdles preventing women from accessing timely healthcare. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why does social isolation within a household make a new mother more vulnerable after childbirth?

options.A: Isolated mothers are legally prohibited from breastfeeding
options.B: The government automatically fines women who do not receive daily visitors
options.C: She lacks practical help and emotional backing, increasing her risk of postpartum depression
options.D: Traditional birth attendants will refuse to visit homes without extended family

explanation: Without a supportive network to share burdens and provide encouragement, new mothers face higher mental health risks. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using a family-centered approach in midwifery?

options.A: To replace trained midwives with senior male family heads
options.B: To transfer hospital administrative duties to teenagers
options.C: To involve household members in supporting safe motherhood practices
options.D: To reduce the total number of children born in every community

explanation: Family-centered care aims to bring relatives on board so they actively support the health of the mother and baby. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is it usually ineffective for a midwife to simply condemn local cultural practices without discussion?

options.A: It is illegal for health workers to express opinions
options.B: It alienates the community and drives families away from formal health facilities
options.C: Traditional customs are always scientifically proven to be safer
options.D: Community elders will immediately close down the clinic

explanation: Disrespecting local traditions makes people defensive, causing them to hide their practices and avoid the clinic altogether. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a common benefit of creating male-friendly spaces at antenatal clinics?

options.A: Men become more involved in financial preparation and birth planning
options.B: Hospital waiting times are permanently reduced to under five minutes
options.C: Fathers take over the physical delivery of babies from midwives
options.D: Pregnant women are completely excused from attending clinic visits

explanation: When clinics welcome men, they learn about pregnancy needs and are more likely to provide funds and transport for delivery. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h6)

question: How can educating influential mothers-in-law improve maternal outcomes in a community?

options.A: They can use their authority within the home to encourage prompt hospital care
options.B: They are required to pay all outstanding medical bills
options.C: They replace community health extension workers during shortages
options.D: They take over legal responsibility for hospital malpractice claims

explanation: Mothers-in-law hold great sway in households; when educated on danger signs, they help ensure women get to the clinic quickly. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which indicator is commonly used to evaluate the success of community maternal health programs?

options.A: The average age of practicing midwives
options.B: The total number of hospital beds painted
options.C: The rate of facility-based deliveries
options.D: The quantity of medical textbooks printed

explanation: Tracking how many women deliver in health facilities is a direct measure of whether community programs are improving birth safety. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the key factor in ensuring a community health program remains sustainable after external funding stops?

options.A: Relocating the health clinic to a major urban city center
options.B: Building genuine community ownership and training local volunteers
options.C: Charging double fees for every emergency service provided
options.D: Importing all medical supplies exclusively from foreign donors

explanation: When local people take charge and are trained to lead, programs can continue running successfully even without outside financial aid. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T2#BMP321_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of your midwifery project defense?

options.A: To memorize every single page of the library
options.B: To rewrite the entire project on a whiteboard
options.C: To prove research competence and clinical value
options.D: To argue with the examiners about statistics

explanation: The defense is a chance to show that your research has practical meaning for patient care and that you understand your work deeply. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do clinical examiners care how your findings relate to actual patient care?

options.A: Hospital management forces them to ask clinical questions
options.B: Theoretical research is banned in Nigerian nursing schools
options.C: Midwifery research must ultimately improve patient care
options.D: Examiners do not care about statistical formulas at all

explanation: As a student midwife, your studies help bridge the gap between classroom theory and real-world improvements in maternal or child health. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which section of the written report outlines the exact study design and sample size used?

options.A: Methodology
options.B: Recommendation
options.C: Table of contents
options.D: Literature review

explanation: The methodology section details how the study was carried out, including the design, population, and sampling techniques. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h2)

question: An examiner points out a mismatch between your sample size and your data table. What is the best step?

options.A: Blame your project typist for changing the numbers
options.B: Refuse to answer questions about the data analysis chapter
options.C: Insist the examiners made a mistake reading the document
options.D: Acknowledge the error calmly and explain the correct figure

explanation: Transparency and professional composure are essential when an error comes up during a review. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of visual slides during your presentation?

options.A: To guide examiners through key points without clutter
options.B: To hide your nervousness behind a bright screen
options.C: To hold every single word of your project report
options.D: To replace the need for an oral presentation

explanation: Visuals should highlight main ideas and data summaries, leaving the detailed narrative to your spoken presentation. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why should you avoid putting long paragraphs of text on presentation slides?

options.A: Long sentences use up too much computer battery power
options.B: It distracts the audience and makes reading difficult
options.C: University guidelines forbid writing more than three lines
options.D: Examiners already know how to read your entire report

explanation: When slides are crowded with text, people stop listening to the speaker and try to read the tiny words instead. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h3)

question: How much time are students usually given for a project presentation before questions begin?

options.A: 10 to 15 minutes
options.B: 1 to 2 hours straight
options.C: As long as the student wants
options.D: Exactly 45 seconds

explanation: Panels set a tight time limit to keep the schedule moving and test your ability to summarize key findings. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the best way to prevent running out of time during your oral presentation?

options.A: Skip the methodology section to save time
options.B: Speak as fast as humanly possible from start
options.C: Practice out loud with a timer beforehand
options.D: Ignore the time warning bells from the panel

explanation: Rehearsals help you adjust your pacing so you comfortably fit all major sections into the allotted timeframe. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h4)

question: How should you respond if an examiner asks about a limitation you did not foresee?

options.A: Argue that the examiner misunderstood your entire project
options.B: Blame your project supervisor for poor guidance
options.C: Pretend you did not hear the question and look away
options.D: Acknowledge the point respectfully and explain your reasoning

explanation: Examiners respect students who handle constructive critique with maturity and professional grace. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate way to handle a question you truly do not know?

options.A: Fabricating false statistics on the spot to sound smart
options.B: Asking the examiner to clarify a specific part of the query
options.C: Pausing briefly to think before giving a cautious answer
options.D: Admitting you will explore that area further after today

explanation: Guessing or making up data ruins your credibility; honesty is always better than fabrication in academic defense. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h5)

question: What attire is expected of a midwifery student during a project defense?

options.A: Neat, professional uniform or formal wear
options.B: Traditional party lace with heavy jewelry
options.C: Casual weekend jeans and a t-shirt
options.D: Lab coat worn over sleeping pyjamas

explanation: A professional appearance shows respect for the academic panel and the nursing and midwifery profession. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h6)

question: An examiner asks a question in a harsh tone. What is your best reaction?

options.A: Raise your voice to match the tone of the examiner
options.B: Report the examiner immediately to the school principal
options.C: Stay calm, remain polite, and answer the academic point
options.D: Burst into tears and run out of the examination hall

explanation: Examiners sometimes use tough questioning styles to test emotional stability and resilience under pressure. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the most important action immediately after receiving corrections from the panel?

options.A: Tear out the corrected pages and rewrite them from memory
options.B: Throw away the notes so you can forget the stressful day
options.C: Wait six months before looking at the project document again
options.D: Record all feedback accurately and consult your supervisor

explanation: Detailed notes ensure you do not miss any required changes before final project binding and submission. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why should examiner feedback be viewed positively rather than as a personal attack?

options.A: It allows the school to charge extra fees for re-binding
options.B: It helps refine your research into a polished academic document
options.C: It has no real impact on your final graduating score
options.D: It means you failed the defense and must repeat the year

explanation: Constructive criticism is designed to improve the accuracy and quality of your final written output. [learn more](BMP321_U3_T3#BMP321_U3_T3_h7)
